Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

nothing pronoun

also nothing at all, nothing new, nothing but, nothing else, have nothing to do, nothing good, nothing bad, nothing useful, nothing ready, absolutely nothing

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: nihil enim scrībis
Cic. Fam. 14.4.4: nihil est quod tē moveat
Traupman 309

nihil

pronoun, indeclinable

With a genitive, “nothing (of)”: nihil novī, nothing new. A second-declension adjective goes into the genitive (nihil malī, nothing bad); a third-declension one agrees (nihil ūtile, nothing useful). “Nothing but” is nihil nisi or nihil aliud nisi (Cic. Amic. 20). “And nothing” is nec quicquam (see anything). Nihil nōn, “nothing not”, is everything (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • nīl — nothing (the contracted form)

    pronoun, indeclinable · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.9.19: nīl habeō quod agam; Plaut. Trin. 4.2.134: nīl agis (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica et cōmica: Plaut., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose (Lewis & Short))

  • nihil prōrsus — absolutely nothing, nothing at all

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.43: inter optimē valēre et gravissimē aegrōtāre nihil prōrsus interesse (Lewis & Short s.v. inter); Traupman 92

Examples

  • hoc igitur habēbis, novī nihil. quid ergō opus erat epistulā?

    so there you have it: nothing new. Then why write a letter at all?Cic. Att. 12.1.2

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    for a long time now I haven’t known how you are, since you write nothingCic. Fam. 7.9.1

  • nīl habeō quod agam et nōn sum piger: ūsque sequar tē

    I’ve nothing to do and I’m not lazy: I’ll follow you all the wayHor. S. 1.9.19

  • nihil est quod tē moveat

    there is nothing to upset youCic. Fam. 14.4.4

  • ‘nihil,’ inquit, ‘longē est deō’

    ‘nothing,’ she said, ‘is far from God’Aug. Conf. 9.11.28

  • est enim amīcitia nihil aliud nisi omnium dīvīnārum hūmānārumque rērum cum benevolentiā et cāritāte cōnsēnsiō

    for friendship is nothing but agreement in all things divine and human, with goodwill and affectionCic. Amic. 20

  • Nihil vērō ūtile, quod nōn idem honestum

    nothing is useful that is not also honourableCic. Off. 3.34

  • nihil umquam malī huic agrō fēcī

    I never did this field any harmPhaedr. App. 28.1–6

  • nihil habeō parātī nisi mē

    I have nothing ready but myselfSen. Ep. 123.1

See also anything, something, no, none, zero, all gone.
